chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Charlie Christian's calm; he fit the new music
summary: Charlie Christian stayed calm about his sudden success, loved to jam, and found in New York the music he had been looking for.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, I guess, you know, he was so young and it was all too much for him, wasn't it?
Yeah. Yeah. Well, he was kind of -- he was very calm about the whole thing. He never got very excited about it. It didn't boil him much.
Didn't it?
No. He was very calm, you know. I never saw Charlie get excited about anything. He took it so -- he took it well, you know. Success came so suddenly.
Yeah.
But it didn't excite him. He just loved to be with us and jam, you know. That's --
Well, music was it all for him.
Yeah. That was the whole thing for him.
Yeah. It's awful sad when guys have got so much and go.
Yeah.
That's a shame. Well, all right, now.
And he understood what we were doing. That's what was so marvelous.
Yeah.
That was the most wonderful thing of all. He seemed to fit right in with what was going on, because, I mean being sort of avant garde, or himself --
Yeah.
That he was sort of looking for something like that.
Yeah.
And it wasn't happening out there.
Where he was,
Where he was, yeah.
Yeah, that's right.
So when he came to New York, he said, 'Wow, that's it,' you know.
